title: Tensor products of fields with one finitely generated extension are Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $K/k$ and $L/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume at least one extension is finitely generated as a field: for example, $K=k(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ for finitely many elements $a_i\in K$, meaning the smallest subfield containing $k$ and these elements is $K$ (or the analogous condition for $L$). Form the commutative ring $T=K\otimes_kL$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$. Then $T$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and Cohen–Macaulay: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$, its localization $T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a Noetherian local ring and satisfies $\operatorname{depth}(T_{\mathfrak q})=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-depth; def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No algebraicity, separability, or perfectness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), statement; Cohen–Macaulay ring is spelled out by its local definition.

proof.text: The swap $K\otimes_kL\to L\otimes_kK$, $u\otimes v\mapsto v\otimes u$, is a ring isomorphism: bilinearity defines it, the tensor multiplication makes it multiplicative, and swapping twice fixes every generator. We may therefore assume $K/k$ is finitely generated as a field.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), symmetry in the two field factors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fg-field-tensor-finite-free-reduction] to $k,K,L$. Choose the resulting finite transcendence basis $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, put $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ and $A=F\otimes_kL$, and let $T=K\otimes_kL$. Its displayed basis gives $T\cong A^d$ with $d\geq1$; in particular $T$ is a finite flat $A$-algebra. The lemma also gives integrality of this global map, without assuming separability.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), proof: choose a finite extension of a purely transcendental extension and form its finite free tensor map.

proof.text: The chosen elements are algebraically independent and generate $F$ as a field, so [lem-trf-rational-field-tensor-local-cm] applies to $F/k$ and $L/k$. It identifies $A$ with $W^{-1}L[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$, where $W$ is the image of the nonzero polynomials over $k$, and proves that $A$ is Noetherian and $\operatorname{depth}(A_{\mathfrak p})=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM), last two sentences of the proof: the rational-field tensor base is a localization of a polynomial ring and is Cohen–Macaulay.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-flat-algebra-local-cm] to the finite flat map $A\to T$ of step 2 and the Noetherian base with the local depth equalities of step 3. It gives Noetherianity of $T$ and, for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset T$ over $\mathfrak p\subset A$, Noetherian local $T_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\operatorname{depth}(T_{\mathfrak q})=\dim T_{\mathfrak q}=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$. These are the required clauses; the swap in step 1 covers finite generation of $L/k$ alone.

source.place: Tag 00R5 (lemma-finite-flat-over-regular-CM), second alternative after prime localization; global finite-flat form used in the proof of Tag 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM).

proof_origin.place: Tag 045M, lemma-tensor-fields-CM, proof; the application of Tag 00R5 is expanded using prime chains (00GT, 00E3), the flat local depth formula (0337), and the depth bound (00LK).
